svg.title: Inspect a found certificate, or record the fresh-lab stop — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Inspect a found certificate, or record the fresh-lab stop
Application server (TLS-APP01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.10
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-app01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
openssl x509 -in /path/to/app.crt \
-noout -dates -subject -issuer
# After Module 6, use the real lab path:
openssl x509 -in /etc/pki/tls/certs/app-v1.crt -noout -dates -subject -issuer -ext subjectAltName
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
When the file exists, notBefore and notAfter are printed along with subject, issuer and
DNS:app.example.mil. Before issuance, file-not-found is an expected stop.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. If you are using our fresh lab, the certificate does not exist yet. Read this example now and run it
after Module 6 installs app-v1.crt.
2. For an existing authorized server, replace /path/to/app.crt with the ssl_certificate path you just
recorded, keeping the rest of the command unchanged.
3. Read notBefore, notAfter, subject and issuer. Then use -ext subjectAltName to inspect names. Only
read public certificates; never substitute a .key path.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
